newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up on late buying ahead of Fed.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up on late buying ahead of Fed.

text.p: Despite several bouts of profit-taking, Thai stocks gained slightly for the third successive day on Thursday as investors bought stocks late, brokers said.
The SET index advanced 2.47 points to 703.09 on 2.7 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index rose 0.32 point to 52.23.

"Local and foreign institutional investors don't want to sell at this level because many are at their target weighting in Thailand. But they at the same time don't want to buy ahead of the US FOMC meeting next week," said a broker at a foreign brokerage house.
Decliners led gainers 153 to 145 while 104 issues unchanged.

Brokers said investors prefered to stay on the sidelines ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting in the United States on Tuesday as some believed it would hike its rates while some did not think so.
They said investors were concerned that already high local rates could be driven up if the U.S. hiked its rates.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, gaining one baht to 118. Advanced Info Services rose eight to 228. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642
